major_findings_require_user_approval: Persistent recovery/quarantine for corrupt or lost Active Project bindings plus transactional writes to the shared binding store (avoid whole-map lost updates across contexts/processes).

History directory ownership and read-only separation so read-only History search does not require metadata write access, plus root-Active-Project scope parity so custom exclusions do not weaken the real-code baseline.
Rejection of changed canonical binding targets (e.g. in-pool symlink replacement) instead of silently following the new target.
limitations: Read-only, time-bounded review: only the three files named in TASK.md were read; no shell, cargo, git, discovery, filesystem scans, installs or skills were run.

The small fix (strip_internal_context on request_permissions echoes) is a low-risk internal-key leak fix and does not address any of the six failing probes; post-fix test results were not available and are not claimed.
History source code (history.rs) was not provided, so findings about history_dir exemptions and metadata-write coupling rest on stderr.log only and need reproduction by the main agent.

Two ToolContext instances writing sequentially is not equivalent to two chats inside one shared context; the lost-update pattern is real but its production likelihood depends on multi-writer deployment.
The symlink retarget probe requires a local filesystem change (replacing a symlink), not a remote-only attack.
The prior advisor run's filesystem search timed out; that run must not be recorded as successful and no full-repo audit is claimed.
No claim of final Codex acceptance is made.
